create.title: Refresh the UG Help screenshot to show clear confirmation and undo
create.body:
Verified during beta testing of the published v1.5 JAR on Windows with Java 25.0.4, against the release guides at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

## Problem

The [Help section](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/UserGuide.md#L427) embeds [helpMessage.png](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/images/helpMessage.png), which describes `clear` as deleting all data and gives `clear` as its example. The pictured general-command sequence also omits `undo`.

## Reproduction and actual behavior

1. Inspect the Help screenshot in the released UG.
2. Launch v1.5 in a disposable folder with records present.
3. Run `help`, then run `clear` in the main window.

The actual Help describes the warning and `clear confirm`. Running `clear` only shows a warning and record counts; no records are deleted. The screenshot gives readers obsolete instructions.

## Fix and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Capture the released Help window and replace `docs/images/helpMessage.png`.
- [ ] Ensure the screenshot shows current clear-confirmation instructions and the undo entry clearly.
- [ ] Check the rendered UG and published image, rather than updating only surrounding Markdown.

This requests a screenshot correction; the implemented clear behavior is correct.

create.title: Correct the release JAR filename in the DG order-editing manual test
create.body:
Verified during beta testing of the published v1.5 JAR on Windows with Java 25.0.4, against the release guides at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

## Problem and reproduction

The [DG order-editing manual test](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/DeveloperGuide.md#L643-L646) instructs readers to launch the release with:

```shell
java -jar "addressbook.jar"
```

Download the v1.5 release into an empty writable folder and run that command. It fails with `Error: Unable to access jarfile addressbook.jar`, because the published asset is named `BakeBase-v1.5.jar`. This prevents readers from reaching the prescribed tests.

## Fix and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use `java -jar "BakeBase-v1.5.jar"` for v1.5, or explicitly tell readers to substitute the downloaded filename.
- [ ] Follow the amended instructions from a clean folder containing the release asset and confirm the app launches.
- [ ] Keep valid references to `addressbook.jar` where they concern local Gradle build output.

The correction concerns the instruction to launch the downloaded release.

create.title: Qualify the UG claim that marked orders remain visible under completion filters
create.body:
Verified during beta testing of the published v1.5 JAR on Windows with Java 25.0.4, against the release guides at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

## Problem

The [mark-order-complete section](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/UserGuide.md#L308) unconditionally states that the order remains visible in the order panel. The [completion-filter section](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/UserGuide.md#L383-L384) correctly says marking removes it from the incomplete view.

## Reproduction

In a disposable empty book:

```text
add-client n/Alpha Baker p/12345678 e/alpha@example.com a/Home
add-item n/Seasonal Tart p/10
add-order 1 i/1 q/1 d/2026-11-03
list-incomplete-orders
mark 1 o/1
list-orders
```

After marking, the stored order count remains one but the incomplete view contains zero orders. `list-orders` shows the completed order again. Filtering works correctly; the unconditional visibility promise can make users think an order unexpectedly disappeared.

## Fix and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replace the unconditional statement with wording such as: “Marking an order does not delete it. It remains visible in the all-orders view, but disappears from the incomplete-orders view. Use list-orders to show all orders again.”
- [ ] Keep the marking and completion-filter sections consistent.
- [ ] Replay the sequence and verify the rendered UG describes both views accurately.

No change to completion-filter behavior is required.

create.title: Replace the DG storage-testing placeholder with executable recovery tests
create.body:
Verified during beta testing of the published v1.5 JAR on Windows with Java 25.0.4, against the release guides at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

## Problem

The [DG data-storage manual-testing subsection](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/DeveloperGuide.md#L622-L628) still contains an authoring placeholder asking the team to explain missing/corrupted-file simulation and expected behavior. It does not provide usable test steps.

This prevents a tester from following the advertised storage-recovery checks and leaves overwrite consequences unexplained.

## Fix and acceptance criteria

Use a disposable writable folder and keep a separate valid backup. Document these cases:

- [ ] **Missing file:** close the app, move `data/addressbook.json` elsewhere, and relaunch. Expect sample data.
- [ ] **Invalid JSON:** close the app, replace the test file contents with an incomplete JSON object such as `{"persons":`, and relaunch. Expect an empty book without a startup crash.
- [ ] **Subsequent save:** run a successful saving command such as `list-clients`. Expect the current fallback book to be written to disk, replacing the missing/invalid file.
- [ ] **Recovery:** close the app, restore a valid backup, and relaunch. Expect its records and associations.
- [ ] Explicitly warn that saving after fallback can overwrite the invalid file; retain backups outside the tested path.
- [ ] Remove the authoring placeholders and execute the documented procedure before publishing.

This is incomplete testing documentation, not a claim that storage recovery itself fails.

update.body:
1. The sequence diagram under the Architecture section shows `delete 1` but `delete` command does not exist. Use `delete-client` instead.
2. The UI component shows PersonListPanel but does not show the panels for bakery items and orders.
3. The sequence diagram under the Logic section shows `delete 1` instead of `delete-client 1`

## Additional v1.5 beta-test evidence

Verified against the released guides and JAR at commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. Suggested PE classification for these documentation discrepancies: `type.DocumentationBug`, `severity.Low`.

Both embedded sequence PNGs still show `delete 1`, although the adjacent prose and command names in their PlantUML sources use `delete-client 1`. The old command returns `Unknown command.` in v1.5.

The logic sequence source additionally shows `DeleteCommand -> Model : deletePerson(1)`. The actual model API takes a resolved `Person`, not an integer.

Evidence:
- [Architecture sequence image](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/images/ArchitectureSequenceDiagram.png)
- [Logic sequence image](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/images/DeleteSequenceDiagram.png)
- [Logic sequence PlantUML source](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/blob/v1.5/docs/diagrams/DeleteSequenceDiagram.puml)

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve the displayed index to a `Person` and label the model call `deletePerson(personToDelete)`, explaining where that variable comes from.
- [ ] Regenerate both sequence PNGs after correcting their PlantUML sources.
- [ ] Inspect the rendered DG to confirm both images use `delete-client 1` and the logic image shows the correct model parameter type.
- [ ] Retain the UI component-panel correction already listed above.

The two PNGs are independently editable; grouping them here is a maintenance choice, not a claim that all related PE reports must be duplicates.
